analysisScope: Client-side React components + API integration patterns

vulnerabilities.description: File upload validation relies only on client-side MIME type checking. Comment mentions 'magic-byte sniff' but implementation only checks file.type property, which can be spoofed. Server must validate actual file content.
vulnerabilities.impact: Attacker could upload malicious files (e.g., executable as PDF)
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Server-side validation with magic-byte verification required (already mentioned in CLAUDE.md as requirement)

vulnerabilities.description: Payment amounts are set client-side (amount = 7900). Although CLAUDE.md states 'Server-side pricing only', this component hard-codes amounts which could theoretically be modified in browser before submission.
vulnerabilities.impact: Client-side amount could be modified before API submission
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Fetch pricing from server endpoint; never calculate amounts client-side. CLAUDE.md confirms server handles pricing correctly.
vulnerabilities.note: Server-side mitigations exist per CLAUDE.md but client-side code is misleading

vulnerabilities.description: Payment gate checked client-side: 'if (!canGenerate)' before attempting generation. While server should enforce this, client-side validation can be bypassed.
vulnerabilities.code: const canGenerate = validation?.isValid && affidavitData?.affiantName && affidavitData?.state && affidavitData?.facts?.length > 0;
vulnerabilities.impact: Determined user could bypass validation checks in browser console
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Server-side validation is primary gate (which exists per CLAUDE.md). Client validation is UX enhancement only.

vulnerabilities.description: Error boundary logs full error details including componentStack to window.logError. If this points to external service, could leak sensitive application architecture and state.
vulnerabilities.code: window.logError({ error: error.toString(), errorInfo: errorInfo.componentStack, userAgent: navigator.userAgent, url: window.location.href });
vulnerabilities.impact: Stack traces and component structure exposed to external service
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Filter error details; never log componentStack. Only log non-sensitive error type and user-friendly message.

vulnerabilities.description: Multiple console.log() statements with detailed debug info remain in production build.
vulnerabilities.code: console.log('🔼 Upload initiated:', { hasFile, documentId, fileName }); console.log('📤 Uploading...'); console.log('📥 Upload response:', data);
vulnerabilities.impact: Debug information visible in production console; aids attacker reconnaissance
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Remove console.log statements or gate behind process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'

vulnerabilities.description: TOS acceptance status stored in localStorage with predictable key (tos_accepted_${user.sub}). localStorage is accessible to any XSS exploit.
vulnerabilities.impact: XSS vulnerability could spoof TOS acceptance by writing to localStorage
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Server-side TOS status is source of truth (confirmed in CLAUDE.md). localStorage is UX optimization only - server validation prevents bypass.

vulnerabilities.description: Auth0 tokens are fetched via getAccessTokenSilently() but NEVER included in subsequent fetch() calls. Per CLAUDE.md, auth uses @auth0/nextjs-auth0 cookie-based session, so tokens aren't needed. Code is confusing and suggests incomplete migration.
vulnerabilities.code: const token = await getAccessTokenSilently(); // ... later: fetch() without Authorization header
vulnerabilities.impact: Code confusion; potential security regression if token was intended
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Remove unused token fetches OR document why tokens are not used. Verify all endpoints rely on cookie auth.

vulnerabilities.description: Draggable item IDs use predictable pattern (fact-0, fact-1, etc.) that can be enumerated.
vulnerabilities.impact: Minimal - IDs are for client-side UI state only, not security-critical
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Use UUID for client-side IDs if security-critical. Current approach acceptable for drag-drop.

codeQualityIssues.description: Inconsistent auth header handling across files
codeQualityIssues.recommendation: Document the auth mechanism (cookie-based per CLAUDE.md) and remove unused token-fetching code

codeQualityIssues.description: Multiple console.log with emoji prefix left in production
codeQualityIssues.recommendation: Strip debug logging or gate behind NODE_ENV check

findings: ✅ Parameterized SQL via lib/db.ts (prevents SQL injection)
✅ RLS enabled at database level (prevents unauthorized data access)
✅ User ownership verified on every authed Route Handler
✅ Stripe webhook uses raw body reading for signature verification (prevents HMAC bypass)
✅ Server-side pricing only (cannot be client-side manipulated)
✅ No hardcoded API keys in client code
✅ Modern dependency versions (Next.js 14, React 18, TypeScript strict)
✅ Uses Zod for input validation on Route Handlers
✅ Stripe SDK used correctly (raw body for webhooks)
✅ No API keys, passwords, or tokens hardcoded
✅ All sensitive config via environment variables
✅ No database credentials in client code

notes: Tooltip parsing in TermsOfServiceModal properly sanitizes keys from TOOLTIP_DEFINITIONS
All user input in forms is escaped by React
Client code contains no SQL queries
All data access via API Route Handlers which use parameterized queries (lib/db.ts)

riskScoreBasis.reasoning: Most security is server-side (RLS, parameterized SQL, ownership checks). Client-side issues are minor (confusing auth code, debug logging, client-side validation redundancy). No hardcoded secrets or critical vulnerabilities.

recommendations.rationale: Code is confusing and suggests incomplete migration from bearer token to cookie auth. Remove or document.
Production builds should not expose debug information
Verify window.logError only receives non-sensitive data
Clarify that server is authoritative source for amounts (client hardcoding is UX only)

recommendations.action: Add code comments explaining server-side validation reliance
recommendations.description: For client-side validation (file types, payment gating, TOS), add comments noting that server performs actual authorization

recommendations.action: Migrate localStorage TOS flag to sessionStorage only
recommendations.rationale: Reduces exposure window of TOS acceptance flag to current session

OWASP_Top10: A01 - Broken Access Control: ✅ Mitigated (RLS + server-side ownership checks)
A02 - Cryptographic Failures: ✅ OK (HTTPS enforced, no sensitive client storage)
A03 - Injection: ✅ Mitigated (parameterized SQL, no dynamic SQL in client)
A04 - Insecure Design: ✅ OK (server-side validation + RLS by design)
A05 - Security Misconfiguration: ⚠️ Review error logging destination
A06 - Vulnerable Components: ✅ Modern deps (no known CVEs at time of analysis)
A07 - Identification Failure: ✅ OK (Auth0 + RLS session management)
A08 - Data Integrity Failures: ✅ OK (Stripe webhook signature verification)
A09 - Logging/Monitoring Failures: ⚠️ Debug logging in production
A10 - SSRF: ✅ OK (API_BASE_URL is relative, no external redirects)

reasoning: Server-side security controls are strong (RLS, parameterized SQL, ownership checks, webhook verification)
No hardcoded secrets or authentication bypass risks
Client-side issues are minor quality/clarity issues, not security holes
Framework choice (Next.js + Auth0) is secure and modern
